title: How far must capital costs move to flip the sand-store versus heat-pump verdict, and is that more than the price year moves it?
summary: Scales the PyPSA technology-data capital costs in the cost model of energy-thermal-real and bisects for the multiplier at which a house-sized sand store and an air-source heat pump cost the same, on real German day-ahead prices 2015–2019. Weekly cycling flips at 1.16, 1.20, 1.20, 0.59 and 1.02 times the store’s table capex, so the table’s own vintage step (1.257×) alone flips four of five years; daily cycling holds to 2.1–3.5×, monthly and seasonal never come close. With capex drawn uniformly within ±h (assumed, swept 0.10–0.50), the spread across price years (sd 0.0063 EUR/kWh) exceeds the cost spread at h = 0.10 (0.0039) and falls below it at h = 0.25 (0.0098). Five years, capex only, wholesale prices; h is an assumption, labelled; all other inputs are sourced.
lede: how far must capex move to flip the sand-store vs heat-pump verdict? Weekly cycling flips on a 2 to 40% store-capex change (the cost table's own vintage step is 26%); daily cycling holds to 2 to 3.5 times.
